§11.2.2 Dual-Axis and Combo Charts

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-dual-axis-and-combo-charts · charts types

✅ Normative

Bars and lines on one canvas, or a second value axis, change only how values are read: each series' values MUST be copied or estimated against its own axis. The chart table is laid out as usual — one row per x position, one column per series — and a series name MUST NOT gain its mark type or axis side (no (line), no right axis).

Before a value is estimated, the axis that scales its series is identified — from the legend order, the mark type and the magnitudes of each axis's tick labels — and the value is traced to that axis. A percentage series scaled by the right-hand axis read against the level axis on the left is a wrong value, however plausible it looks.

✅ Sample — industrial-group-financial-report-2024_p15

Two bar series in euros and a percentage line share one canvas; no value axis is drawn, and every mark prints its value, so every cell is copied rather than read. Full coverage is 15 values under the legend entries, copied whole (Earnings per share (EUR) keeps the parenthesis printed inside the legend). The chart prints decimal commas (2,08, 48,1%), and the cells keep them. The earnings values are printed in bold.

Expected Markdown
